source_window.data_date: current product accessed 2026-10-02; updated every six weeks

field_evidence.uprn_semantics: OS Open UPRN provides a Unique Property Reference Number for every addressable location in Great Britain.
field_evidence.coordinate_semantics: The product provides coordinate references associated with each UPRN so records can be spatially analysed and visualised.
field_evidence.authority: Ordnance Survey states that UPRNs are primarily allocated by Local Authorities under their legal duty to maintain this information.
field_evidence.update_cadence: The product is updated every six weeks.
field_evidence.data_structure: Vector product available as CSV and GeoPackage.
field_evidence.parcel_limitation: The product page describes addressable-location identifiers and coordinates, not cadastral/title parcel polygons.

first_missing_criterion: Verified BUILDING_PRESENT canonical parcel geometry/bbox for this producer. Ordnance Survey's official OS Open UPRN product supplies authoritative UPRN identifiers with coordinate references for addressable locations, but it does not supply cadastral/title parcel polygons. A UPRN location point cannot be promoted to canonical parcel geometry or bbox. Local OpenCode must bind the target-specific BUILDING_PRESENT record to a canonical parcel/title polygon; after that, bind one exact official DEM/LIDAR tile or metadata-index record to the resulting bbox.
exact_blocker: The official Ordnance Survey OS Open UPRN product is a materially different identifier-and-location source from the prior OS OpenMap–Local building-polygon window. It provides authoritative UPRNs and coordinate references for addressable locations and is free to use, but it is an addressable-location identifier dataset rather than a cadastral/title parcel polygon dataset. Therefore it cannot satisfy the canonical parcel geometry/bbox prerequisite for Height Difference. No target-specific canonical parcel binding exists in the verified lineage, so accepted/materialized/direct parcel counts remain zero and spatial join/materialization remains local OpenCode work.
